subject: QuantumEdge activation runway — feature-reserve & evaluation shim
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamie Park <jamie@quantumedge.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: QuantumEdge activation runway — initial ask

Irene / Marissa — quick one. QuantumEdge (Jamie cc'd) is at the final stages of procurement but they have one hard dependency: per-tenant KV cache pinning and a deterministic fallback for cold-residency requests. They want a short EAP window where we guarantee residency for a small set of high-value tenants while we validate throughput.

High-level ask: can Eng/Product commit to a temporary "activation shim" (best-effort pin + fallback to a lower-latency variant) for QEDGE-1 tenants for the pilot? Key constraints:
- Timeline: pilot needs to start week of 3/23 (customer kickoff 3/30)
- Scope: pin up to 10 tenants, lightweight config flag per-tenant, observable metrics and a rollback path
- Risk tolerance: internal SLOs can be relaxed for pilot month but we need clear runbook and an automatic fallback if token latency > 250ms 95th

I've attached the MOP and the procurement conversation for context (quantumedge_activation_mop.pdf).

Next steps: can we get a nod on feasibility + a rough engineering estimate by EOD Wed 3/4? If yes, Marissa can bake this into the product gating for a targeted EAP.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0188

Attachment: quantumedge_activation_mop.pdf

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Jamie Park <jamie@quantumedge.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QuantumEdge activation runway — initial ask

Thanks Ben — quick technical read. Short answer: we can do a temporary shim but need to be explicit about tradeoffs.

Questions / items we need from sales/customer before engineering estimates:
1) Which API surface will the customer use to select pinned tenants? (tenant_id vs. external_customer_id)
2) Expected QPS and P95 token latencies for pinned tenants during peak — example numbers help sizing
3) Who is the rollback owner at the customer (for fast kills)?

Notes on implementation options (very high level):
- Option A (fast): config flag + best-effort pin at routing layer. Low engineering time (~2-3 sprints) but no strict guarantees under global contention. Automatic fallback to compatible model variant on overload.
- Option B (stronger): dedicate warm pool capacity + placement affinity. Higher cost/infra and ~4-6 sprints.

If Sales can confirm the API key mapping and provide the peak numbers, I can sketch a narrow-scope Option A MOP and estimate by Wed EOD. Looping in Jasmine for deployment/runbook input.

Irene
Irene Choi | Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
irene.choi@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Jamie Park <jamie@quantumedge.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QuantumEdge activation runway — initial ask

Appreciate the quick triage. I think we can aim for Option A as a bridge — product is OK with a limited-scope EAP with explicit guardrails. Proposal:
- Product commitment: support Option A for up to 10 tenants, feature gated behind an EAP flag
- Engineering commitment: delivery of MOP + deployment automation + telemetry for pilot (target: 3 sprints, with a prioritized sprint slice for the shim)
- Success criteria: <5% error rate on pinned traffic and 95th latency under 300ms for pilot workload; otherwise auto-disable
- Documentation: a minimal runbook and rollback instructions (owner: Jasmine)

Tradeoffs to surface to customer: this is not a long-term SLA-backed residency — it's a time-bound pilot to de-risk migration. If they want production guarantees, we need to move to dedicated warm pools (Option B) and a commercial commitment.

Ben — can you ask QuantumEdge to sign the attached one-page MOU (we only need a signed acknowledgment of the pilot scope and acceptance of the relaxed SLOs) and confirm the tenant selection list by 3/11? If they sign, we'll prioritize a sprint slice for the 3/23 kickoff planning.

Marissa Cole | Group PM, Enterprise Features
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attachment: (please sign) quantumedge_activation_mop.pdf

From: Jamie Park <jamie@quantumedge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, contracts@quantumedge.com
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QuantumEdge activation runway — initial ask

Thanks everyone — this looks reasonable and pragmatic. We discussed internally and agree to proceed with the EAP (Option A) under the pilot terms you outlined.

Action items from our side:
- I've attached the signed one-page MOU (quantumedge_mou_signed.pdf).
- Procurement will send a short PO confirmation next week; procurement contact is contracts@quantumedge.com.
- I'll provide the tenant list and expected peak QPS by 3/11.

We appreciate the flexibility — please proceed with the MOP and let us know any blocker items.

— Jamie Park
VP Product, QuantumEdge Inc.
jamie@quantumedge.com
Attachment: quantumedge_mou_signed.pdf
